display.title: Episode 298: The King and the Shabbos Candles
display.summary_short: Right after Sukkos: the Ushpizin and the joy of Hakafos, the story of a king saved by a Shabbos candle, and a call for every girl to light her own Shabbos candle.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week after Sukkos 5748. Uncle Yossi looks back on the sukkah, the four kinds and the dancing of Hakafos, and explains that just as Eliyahu HaNavi visits the Seder, the seven holy guests, Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov and the others, visit the sukkah each night with blessings that reach us through more Torah and mitzvos. After the Hakochainik march, two sisters from Beis Rivkah lead the Shema. Story time tells of a king who banned all candles after a candle burned down his new study. The Jews prayed and took on to have every mother and daughter light Shabbos candles, and when the king was lost in a snowstorm on a Friday night, the light of a Shabbos candle in a cabin outside the city saved his life, so he cancelled the decree. Uncle Yossi then teaches that children are their parents' greatest treasure, that Torah and mitzvos are light, and that girls bring their parents true nachas by lighting their own Shabbos candle, with a gift and a candlestick offered to first-time lighters. The show ends with a listener's Rosh Hashanah letter.
display.lesson: Torah and mitzvos are light; a girl who lights her own Shabbos candle brings light to her home and true nachas to her parents.
